DigestMultibase.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.

Response.title: VTC Join Requests — Vetting — Show — response payload

VettingFacts.description: What the community established about a request's vetting evidence when it decided — the join policy's vetting input, in lowerCamelCase.

applicantDigestMatches.description: The applicant named the same `requirementsDigest` — they applied under the version of the requirements that was applied.

commitmentsConsistent.description: Every counted statement carries the same identity commitment.

criterionId.description: The Accepts criterion whose requirements were applied.

distinctCountedVetters.description: Distinct eligible vetters counted, each once however many DIDs they hold.

needs.description: What was still missing, in the `vetting:*` grammar. Empty when `satisfied`.

satisfied.description: Count, method floors, consistency and independence all held.

VettingFacts.title: VettingFacts

VettingMethod.description: How the vetter established that the person they checked is the person controlling the applicant's DID. `inPerson` — both people were physically together. `video` — a live, two-way video call. `priorAcquaintance` — the vetter has known or worked with this person over a period, and attests from that knowledge rather than from a document. A method is a description of what happened, not an assurance level: which methods count, and how many of each, is community policy.
VettingMethod.title: VettingMethod

VettingRelationship.description: The vetter's own declaration of how they relate to the applicant. Declared, not verified: it exists so community policy can cap how much evidence comes from people close to the applicant, and a false declaration is the vetter's attributable act.
VettingRelationship.title: VettingRelationship

VettingStatementFacts.description: One identity-vetting statement the applicant's presentation carried, as the community saw it at the decision — plus whether its vetter has withdrawn it since.

eligible.description: Its issuer was an eligible vetter at the decision.

failures.description: Why it did not count, as machine codes in the `vetting:*` grammar the join policy reads. Empty when it counted.

id.description: The statement's `id`, when it had one.

issuer.description: The vetter who issued it, when it could be read.

revoked.description: Withdrawn by its vetter before the decision.

verified.description: Its proof, type, validity window and body verified.

withdrawnNow.description: Withdrawn by its vetter now — after the decision, when `revoked` is false. Read live, not recorded.

VettingStatementFacts.title: VettingStatementFacts
